speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with a concerning rash and recent health changes; to begin our assessment, have you noticed any fever, chills, or unexplained weight loss accompanying the rash?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old male. The patient presents with a rash that started last night, finding it very concerning. He does not recall being exposed to any new environmental stimuli such as detergents or plants like poison ivy. He mentions he recently started seeing a primary care provider for arthritis management and a new onset cough.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The patient mentions recent onset of cough and seeing a provider for arthritis; are you currently experiencing joint pain or morning stiffness? Also, have you noticed any shortness of breath with the cough?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, CRP.
REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray.

speaker: Doctor
text: The initial blood work and chest X-ray came back with normal readings. Given your recent cough and joint pain, along with this new rash, could you describe exactly where the rash is located and whether it appears in specific patterns, such as on your knuckles or in the webs of your fingers?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on the upper half of the back. I also have Concern over sudden onset, Recent cough, Unaware of exposure to new environmental stimuli, Mucositis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Sarcoidosis (likely Löfgren syndrome variant or pulmonary sarcoidosis with cutaneous involvement).

The combination of a new cough, joint pain, and a specific rash on the upper back (potentially erythema nodosum) strongly suggests this systemic granulomatous disease. Do you have any difficulty swallowing or a white coating on your tongue, which might indicate the mucositis you mentioned?
